chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the minimum upon which zakat becomes obligatory from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. So he said: Five awsaq, by the wasq of the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).
So I said: How much is the wasq? He said: Sixty sa'as.
I said: Is there then zakat on grapes, or does it only become obligatory when one turns them into raisins? He said: Yes, when it is estimated (by valuation), its zakat is to be taken out.

key_terms.أَوْسَاق: Awsaq: plural of wasq, an agricultural measure equal to 60 sa'as (approx. 130 kg of grain)
key_terms.خَرْص: Khars: formal estimation/valuation of the anticipated yield of a farm crop by an assessor
key_terms.صَاع: Sa': dry measure, approximately 2.17 liters or 2.5-3 kg depending on the commodity
key_terms.وَسْق: Wasq: unit of dry measure used in zakat law, calibrated to prophetic standards

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum nisab for zakat on wheat, barley, dates, and raisins according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: In this jurisprudential dialogue, Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari questions Imam al-Ridha (AS) about the nisab (minimum threshold) for zakat on four categories of agricultural produce: wheat, barley, dates, and raisins. The Imam specifies five awsaq — a standard unit equal to sixty sa'as per wasq, totaling 300 sa'as — as the nisab, calibrated to the measure used by the Prophet (SAWW). The Imam further rules that zakat on grapes applies when they are in the grape state (estimated by khars, a formal valuation), not only after drying. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential position that zakat applies to grapes themselves at harvest, distinguished from the Sunni view that zakat applies only to dried raisins.
word_analysis: awsaq (pl. of wasq, a unit of measure)

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad Al Ashary who said, ‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the least what would Obligated the Zakāt, from the wheat, and the barley, and the dates, and the raisins. So heasws said: ‘Five Owsaaq by the Wasaq of the Prophetsaww’.
So I said, ‘How much is the Wasaq?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sixty Sa’as’.
I said, ‘So is there Zakāt upon the grapes, or rather it would be Obligated upon it when it does become a raisin’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, when it is estimated, its Zakāt would be taken out’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash’ariy who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the minimum Zakat due on wheat, barley, dates and raisins. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is one wasaq out of five Awsaq of wasq of the Holy prophet.’
I then asked, ‘How much is wasaq?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is sixty Sa‘.’
I then asked, ‘Is there Zakat on grapes or that there is Zakat on it only when it is turned into raisins. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, when he estimates it then pays its Zakat.’”
